claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

informal_arrangement.description: Whether the claimant is looking after someone else's child through an informal arrangement.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me here at home. I'm wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know about Alex, who is 8 years old and lives with you at home.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask you a few more questions:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. That's helpful information.

Now I need to understand a bit more about your situation:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care? By this I mean, do you provide for his daily needs such as food, clothes, and other expenses?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, yes, I look after him day-to-day - I make sure he's fed, clothed, and taken care of. He lives with me full-time, so I'm the one looking after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's very helpful, thank you. It sounds like you are responsible for Alex's care.

I have a few more questions to make sure I have a complete picture:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or in any residential accommodation, or has he been for an extended period?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that. He's just at home with me - he's not in hospital or care or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Now I need to ask:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, such as another parent or guardian?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Do you have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or are you a British citizen, or do you have another immigration status that gives you the right to reside in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm sorry, but I don't have information about my immigration status. That wasn't something I was told about in my situation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's perfectly understandable. Let me ask a different question that might help:

**Were you born in the UK, or have you always lived in the UK, or have you moved to the UK from another country?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm sorry, but I don't have that information either. I only know that I currently live in the UK - I wasn't given any details about my background or how long I've been here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - thank you for letting me know. 

Let me ask one final question to complete my assessment:

**Has Alex started any paid work (24 hours or more per week), or is he claiming any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's only 8 years old, so he's not working at all, and he's not claiming any benefits himself. He's just a regular kid going to school.
